projects.name: survey-product-detail-page
projects.role: Survey product detail page built from Project Aura DS section components on Next.js; a reference for how a long product page composes DS sections and cards.
notes: Large Next.js + Tailwind v4 app with its own .git. Most styling is Tailwind utility classes inside TSX; the tsx-classes pattern kind is not implemented by this module, so only the hand-written rules in src/app/globals.css are catalogued.
src/vendor/ holds a vendored COPY of the design system and its tokens. That copy is not the DS: never read DS values from it.
--bg-pure-white is redefined to a translucent white inside the cinematic HeroSection scope, so any rule that reads it (for example the .pdp-card background) is not catalogued.

The --pdp-card-* tokens exist only in this project, so the colours are not used by name: the 6% border maps to the nearest suitable DS hairline token and the two-layer shadow to the DS card shadow (the dropped 2% layer is recorded). The 10px radius is a hardcoded length, so the card verifies as a proposed local variant.

patterns.purpose: Light separation of a card from the page with a 6%-alpha hairline border and a faint two-layer shadow
patterns.description: Rest state of the canonical .pdp-card (derived from the Report Store Card, per its source comment): 10px radius, 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.06) border, 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.04) plus 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.02) shadow. Background, hover lift and transition are not catalogued.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not inside the cinematic/dark hero scope. Not when a flat card with no shadow at all is wanted (use competition-benchmarking-v2-react flat-hairline-card). Its tokens exist only in this project, so applying it yields a proposed local variant, never an official DS component.

projects.name: case-study-v2
projects.role: Case-study page with five switchable templates (A to E) on Next.js; a composition reference for case-study heroes, stat strips and timelines.
notes: All styling is one hand-written src/app/globals.css built on project-local tokens (--ink, --slate, --mist, --smoke, --fog, --surface, --red ...) that are not DS tokens, with a dev template switcher.
No pattern is catalogued: no rule is both DS-grounded and clearly reusable, and the project-local palette would only ever verify as hardcoded values.

projects.name: ken-auth-redesign
projects.role: Loop-engineering paper trail for the sign-up / sign-in modal redesign: PROJECT.md, README.md, specs/, comparisons/ and a Next.js build under builds/.
notes: Not a src app at the project root: it is a docs/specs/builds/comparisons folder (references/ and renders/ are empty). The runnable app lives in builds/ and depends on workspace packages that are not in the folder.

builds/src/app/globals.css is only 54 lines (Tailwind source, body and a token mapping) and the screens are styled with Tailwind classes, so there are no CSS rules to catalogue. Consult specs/ and builds/src/components only for AuthModal/OTP composition when the DS has no suitable form-field treatment.

projects.name: expert-interview-page
projects.role: Expert-interview page as plain static HTML (index.html plus assets); a layout reference for interview/quote-driven pages.
notes: Plain static HTML with embedded <style> blocks and no TypeScript source. The html-style pattern kind is not implemented by this module, so nothing is catalogued.

projects.name: report-store-legacy
projects.role: Frozen Report Store UI (Vite/React, Figma Make export, marked LEGACY-READONLY.md): visual truth for older Report Store treatments such as cards, filters and the icon badge.
notes: LEGACY-READONLY: frozen 2026-05-08, never edited. Consult it only after the DS and competition-benchmarking-v2-react have no suitable treatment.
A same-named folder also exists at design-system-audit/worked-examples/report-store-legacy. It is NOT approved; resolution rejects it because its realpath is not this folder.
Components are Tailwind v4 classes in TSX (tsx-classes is not implemented by this module) plus src/styles/theme.css tokens, so no hand-written CSS rule is catalogued.

projects.name: competition-benchmarking-v2-react
projects.role: PREFERRED reference for subtle borders and light section/card separation: a Vite 6 + React 19 + TypeScript report page whose entire styling is src/globals.css, using soft black-alpha hairlines and flat cards instead of heavy boxy outlines.
notes: User preference (2026-10-09): when an authorized change needs a subtle border or light card/section separation, consult this project first and avoid heavy outlines.

All styling is src/globals.css: two :root blocks (design tokens, plus the .v1-* card tokens) and plain class rules. The catalogued rules were read from that file and are re-checked against it on every verification.

globals.css is a self-contained copy of Aura tokens, not an import of the DS package. A colour is never taken by its token name: it is read (alpha included) and mapped by VALUE to the DS token for the same role on the same surface. --border-soft, --tint-soft and --white carry the same values in the DS editorial-light scope (exact matches); --border-strong (15%) is NOT the DS --border-strong (18%) and maps to --border-input; --faq-border (#f5f5f5) maps exactly to a DS colour-ramp primitive.

A rule inside @media / @supports applies only when its condition holds for the need (prefers-color-scheme against the surface, width queries against the viewport); otherwise the base rule is read and the property is marked as conditioned. Only declarations that no media query overrides are catalogued; layout declarations of the same selectors (padding, flex direction, grid columns) are the page's own and are deliberately left out.

patterns.purpose: Light separation of a card from its section: a flat white card with a soft hairline border and small radius, no shadow and no heavy outline
patterns.description: The shared .v1-card shell used by the Action Plan, Next Steps and Execution Plan cards: white fill, 1px --border-soft (rgba(0,0,0,.08)) border, --radius-sm (10px) corners, no box-shadow.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not on dark surfaces (a black 8% hairline disappears on dark fills). Not where a card must read as elevated or interactive: it has no shadow and no hover state. Not when the DS Card already provides the required treatment.

patterns.purpose: Light separation of a callout or contact panel from a plain section: a barely tinted fill inside a soft hairline border
patterns.description: The FAQ contact panel (.faq-contact): --tint-soft (rgba(0,0,0,.03)) fill, 1px --border-soft border, --radius-sm corners. Only the surface treatment is catalogued; its padding, margins and flex layout are the page's own.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not on dark surfaces. Not for content cards that should read as white on a tinted band (use flat-hairline-card). Do not take spacing or layout from this rule; those declarations are specific to the FAQ panel.

patterns.purpose: Separate a row of figures from the rest of the section with two soft hairline rules instead of a boxed outline
patterns.description: The executive-summary KPI strip (.es-kpi-strip): bounded above and below by 1px --border-soft rules, with no side borders, fill or radius. An open editorial treatment that is deliberately not a card.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not where the content needs a closed container, and not on dark surfaces. The column rules between items and the responsive reflow of the original strip are separate rules and are not part of this pattern.

patterns.purpose: Question-and-answer accordion row separated by a very faint hairline border with rounded, clipped corners
patterns.description: The FAQ row shell (.faq-row): 1px --faq-border (#f5f5f5) border, --radius-sm corners, overflow hidden so the collapsing answer is clipped to the rounded shell. The question button, chevron and grid-rows collapse are separate rules and are not catalogued.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not where the boundary must stay visible for contrast: #f5f5f5 is nearly invisible on white. Not a complete accordion; it carries none of the button, chevron or expand/collapse behaviour.

patterns.purpose: The project's ladder of black-alpha hairline border colours for subtle borders: soft 8%, default 12%, strong 15%, active 20%
patterns.description: Custom properties on :root behind every hairline in the project. --border-soft is the one used for card and section separation; --border-default for firmer dividers and some card outlines; --border-strong is commented as the input-hover border; --border-active as the focused or emphasised border.
patterns.whenNotToUse: These are literal alpha values of this project, not DS tokens: use them to choose or compare against a DS border token and do not copy them as magic numbers. Not for dark surfaces (see hairline-border-on-dark).

patterns.purpose: The project's hairline border colour for dark surfaces: white at 14% alpha
patterns.description: Custom property --border-on-dark on :root. It is declared in this project but no rule reads it yet, so it has not been seen in a rendered dark section here.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Not on light surfaces. Treat it as a candidate value only: it is unused and unverified in a rendered dark section, and it is a literal value of this project rather than a DS token.
